episodes.177568: Early evening severe thunderstorms produced numerous reports of large hail.
episodes.177612: A strong cold front crossed Pennsylvania during the afternoon and evening of April 5, 2023, accompanied by scattered showers and thunderstorms. A few gusty storms formed in the high shear/low-CAPE environment, and one storm produced minor wind damage in Somerset County. This activity weakened as is progressed eastward across central Pennsylvania and into a more stable environment.
episodes.177650: A cold front moved through the afternoon of April 5th. Elevated convection behind the front led to several showers and thunderstorms the evening of April 5th. Some of the thunderstorms produced hail the size of pennies and quarters across northern Jim Hogg County in and around Hebbronville between 9:25PM CDT and 9:45PM CDT.
episodes.177712: A cold front spawned several severe thunderstorms that resulted in localized hail and wind damage.

episodes.177715: A cold front spawned several thunderstorms that resulted in up to near hurricane force wind gusts over area waterways.
episodes.178401: An upper low pressure system over the Four Corners Region ejected northeast through the Southern Rockies into the Central Plains by the afternoon of April 5th, which reinforced a cold front southeast into East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana before stalling out late in the day. Large scale ascent increased along and ahead of the front and the ejecting upper low, which had tapped into a warm and moderately unstable air mass that had pooled north from the Gulf of Mexico ahead of the front. This resulted in numerous shower and thunderstorm development during the morning around and after daybreak over Northeast Texas and Southwest Arkansas, which eventually moved into portions of extreme Northwest Louisiana by late morning/early afternoon. Some of these storms became severe, with damaging winds observed and even an isolated tornado briefly touching down just west of Linden in Cass County Texas. While these storms eventually weakened by mid-afternoon, additional redevelopment occurred along the slowing front farther south of I-20 in East Texas by late afternoon and early evening as they tapped stronger instability, with isolated severe thunderstorms producing large hail affecting portions of Cherokee and Panola Counties before moving into extreme Northwest Louisiana.
episodes.178403: An upper low pressure system over the Four Corners Region ejected northeast through the Southern Rockies into the Central Plains by the afternoon of April 5th, which reinforced a cold front southeast into East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana before stalling out late in the day. Large scale ascent increased along and ahead of the front and the ejecting upper low, which had tapped into a warm and moderately unstable air mass that had pooled north from the Gulf of Mexico ahead of the front. This resulted in numerous shower and thunderstorm development during the morning around and after daybreak over Northeast Texas and Southwest Arkansas, which eventually moved into portions of extreme Northwest Louisiana by late morning/early afternoon. Some of these storms became severe, with damaging winds and large hail observed. While these storms eventually weakened by mid-afternoon, additional redevelopment occurred along the slowing front farther south of I-20 in East Texas and North Louisiana by late afternoon and early evening as they tapped stronger instability, with isolated severe thunderstorms producing large hail affecting portions of Western Caddo Parish before weakening.
episodes.178408: A slow moving cold front drifted south across East Texas and North Louisiana south of the Interstate 20 corridor during the morning hours of April 6th. Abundant moisture from the Gulf and the Southern Pacific continued to stream northeast along and behind the front, south of an upper low that shifted northeast into the Central Plains. This moisture enhanced rain rates, with embedded thunderstorms developing and moving repeatedly over the same areas. Widespread rainfall amounts of 3-5 inches fell across much of Deep East Texas and Northwest Louisiana from the 5th to the 7th, atop already saturated grounds from much above normal rainfall received during the winter and early springtime months. This resulted in areas of flash flooding across portions of Bossier and Desoto Parishes, before the rains gradually ended as the front shifted south out of the area and drier air spilled south in its wake.

episodes.178455: Unsettled weather conditions prevailed due to an upper level cut-off low strengthening northwest of the islands. The divergence aloft was strong enough to support small hail over the Virgin Islands.
episodes.178482: Large hail up to golf ball size fell and trees and power lines were downed by severe thunderstorms that developed in advance of an approaching cold front.
episodes.178511: Thunderstorms developed in advance of an approaching cold front. Some of these increased to severe levels and produced very large hail, some stones up to tennis ball size, and also localized damaging wind gusts.
episodes.178735: A strong upper level weather disturbance tapped into an unusually moist airmass to produce heavy rain with embedded thunderstorms in the Finger Lakes region of New York.
episodes.178736: A strong upper level weather disturbance tapped into an unusually moist airmass to produce heavy rain with embedded thunderstorms in the Finger Lakes region of New York.
episodes.178946: The WI River at Portage was in flood much of the month of April from the combination of snowmelt and precipitation in the middle to upper basins of the river. The river reached moderate flood stage and was just short of reaching major flood stage.
episodes.179181: The center of a closed upper-level low advanced just west of the Great Lakes on the evening of April 5th. An organized line of convection developed ahead of the cold front and created strong winds and isolated tornadoes from eastern Illinois to eastern Ohio. DCAPE values will likely near air above 1000J/kg with high cloud based ceilings prior to convection. Hi-Res model guidance also suggested that effective shear ranged between 30-40kts.
episodes.179184: Showers and thunderstorms ahead of a cold front moving in from the northwest developed over the Eastern Shore of Maryland, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.179249: Afternoon thunderstorms transpired on April 4th and 5th as the result of strong southerly flow ushering in warmer than average temperatures into West Virginia. Storms on the 4th had the capability of producing one inch hail in Lincoln County, while on the 5th damaging wind gusts were the main culprit behind downed trees in Harrison and Taylor Counties.
episodes.179359: An area of repeated thunderstorms moved across portions of the Mohawk Valley during the evening hours on April 5, 2023 into the overnight hours on April 6 resulting in a couple of debris flows from the heavy rainfall.
episodes.179442: Warm air advection above a cooler airmass behind a cold front generated elevated thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced large hail.
episodes.179443: Warm air advection above a cooler airmass generated elevated thunderstorms. Training of storms led to locally heavy rainfall and minor flooding.
episodes.179583: Storm force west-southwest wind gusts developed on the 5th and 6th around a deepening low pressure system over the Upper Great Lakes.
episodes.179590: A persistent zone of deep layer shear over the Gulf Coast region and moderate mid level lapse rates produced conditions somewhat favorable for large hail.
episodes.179725: Clusters of showers and thunderstorms developed along an in advance of a cold front during the late afternoon into the early evening hours across the northwest Piedmont. A cluster of storms become severe and produced damaging winds across Davidson County, along with sub-severe hail across Davidson and Forsyth Counties.
episodes.179834: Isolated thunderstorms developed over the Victoria Crossroads ahead of a cold front in the early evening hours. Thunderstorm produced quarter to ping pong ball sized hail east of Victoria.
episodes.179861: An impulse of moisture traversing mid-level flow introduced chances for isolated shower and thunderstorms for areas south of I-20. The morning sounding showed substantial capping at 600 mb, however lapse rates were quite steep between 400 and 600 mb. As much of 1500 -2000 J/Kg of CAPE was possible by the afternoon. Due to these conditions, a few storms were able to develop gusty winds and some hail.
episodes.179935: A stalled surface boundary was draped over the the northwestern portions of the area during the afternoon hours. In the early afternoon, storms began to develop in response to the improving instability and one dominant cell emerged along the boundary over southwest Mississippi. At peak intensity, the cell produced quarter sized hail in Wilkinson and Amite county in southwest Mississippi before weakening as it moved off of the boundary to the east-northeast.
episodes.179978: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of central Virginia and the Virginia northern neck.
episodes.179986: Scattered severe thunderstorms in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds and large hail across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.180016: Scattered thunderstorms developed across the North Carolina Piedmont during the late afternoon. One isolated severe storm produced large hail north of I-40.
